certificate: ✓ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 400 s after acceptance (F4)

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The cancellation was made by the rider (F4), so NS-0 routes this case to NS-4: an on-demand booking cancelled within 3 minutes of matching is not chargeable, and only a cancellation after 3 minutes makes the $6.61 fee valid.

The rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after acceptance at 08:46:40 (F4), which is beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so under NS-4 the $6.61 cancellation fee stands and the correct outcome on the fee itself is no_action.

The fee could only be avoided by attacking the charge as a driver-claimed no-show, but this is not a driver-cancellation no-show case at all: the driver never engaged the no-show route, so NS-1/NS-2 are not alternative routes to relief here (F4, F12).

The rider's own reason — 'plans changed' (F11) — is a voluntary change of mind, not a driver fault or a Ryde rule breach, and Ryde's published rule gives no fee waiver for a change of plans after 3 minutes (F4).
No rule-based fee reduction is available: the charge is exactly the published $6.61 (F8) with no surge (F9) and no unknown add-on, so FARE-1 discloses nothing to refund.

Because the actionable amount under the policy is zero, the substantive decision on this ticket must be no_action, and the rider's only remaining avenue is the goodwill/human channel in NS-7, which permits a waiver request within 30 days and issues any refund as a voucher, not cash (F4, F8).
The rider's account shows no pattern of fee abuse — 1 dispute in 90 days and 0 upheld (F16) — so nothing in the profile supports extra adverse treatment of the rider in this file.

weaknesses: The timestamps defeat the fairness argument: cancellation at 08:46:40 is 6 min 40 s after the 08:40:00 acceptance (F4), squarely outside NS-4's 3-minute free window, so the $6.61 is contractually valid.
The rider's own chat message 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' (F11) is a direct admission of voluntary cancellation and explains why no fee waiver is available under the published rules.

The driver was in fact available and waiting: within 200 m from 08:41:35, 39 m away at 08:42:40, and stationary 41 m from pickup for 4 min 40 s until the cancellation (F1, F2, F3, F6), with a matching 'I'm here' chat at 08:42 (F10) — this rebuts any suggestion of driver non-attendance and undercuts the complaint’s premise.
NS-8 (other operators' ETA-based free cancellation) is informational and 不可引用, and Ryde publishes no such rule, so it cannot be cited to waive the fee.
The driver's own record (F17: 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) does not help the rider and, if anything, cut the other way on credibility of any arrival complaint.

claims.assertion: The rider, not the driver, cancelled this instant RydeX booking: she cancelled at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after acceptance at 08:40:00, so the free-cancellation window (first 3 minutes after matching) had already closed and the $6.61 cancellation fee is validly charged.

The rider's own words confirm she cancelled for a personal reason and not because of any driver failure: at 08:45 she wrote 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel', while the system shows the driver was already at the pickup.

Even judged under the driver-no-show / rider-no-show standard, the driver met every arrival requirement: he was first within 200 m of the pickup at 08:41:35, tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 39 m from the pickup point, and remained within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap (5 min 5 s cumulative before cancellation).

The driver was physically waiting at the pickup: he was stationary at 41 m from the pickup point for 4 min 40 s (08:42:00–08:46:40), and his closest approach was 39 m at 08:42:40, so the rider's claim that 'the driver had not even arrived' is contradicted by the GPS record.

The driver's waiting was real and communicated: he messaged at 08:42 'I'm here at the pickup, black Hyundai Ioniq', consistent with the stationarity record, so the rider's change of plans cost the driver a completed trip after he had fully performed his side.

No route, traffic or weather factor excuses the rider: there were no traffic incidents or speed-band records on the route and weather was fair, so the only reason for the cancellation was her changed plans.
The rider has a history of raising disputes (1 dispute in 90 days, 0 upheld), which supports that this fee complaint is unfounded rather than a systemic driver failure.

weaknesses: The fact index contains contradictory entries on the 'I'm Here' tap: F6 (timeline) records a tap at 08:42:15, but F7 (timeline) states 'Driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null)'. The rider's side will cite F7 to argue the arrival/NS-1 conditions fail, and under the system-records rule the judge will weigh the two timeline records.

The rider will also rely on the fact that this is her personal plan change and that she cancelled only 6 min 40 s after acceptance — if the rider's NS-4 reading is accepted, the fee stands, but she may invoke NS-7's 30-day RydeHELP waiver request to seek a discretionary voucher.

The driver's 90-day history shows 1 upheld no-show dispute (F17), so the rider may ask the judge to treat the account as having a prior no-show finding and to flag it, even though this case's facts show full driver performance.

points.response: Conceded on the fee mechanics: the rider cancelled at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after the 08:40:00 acceptance (F4), past NS-4's 3-minute window, so the $6.61 stands on the record (F8) and I do not ask the judge to disturb it.
Conceded: F11 ('Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel') is my client's own admission and I will not argue driver failure as the cause of the cancellation.

Conceded that the arrival conditions in NS-1 are met on the timeline records — F6 records an 'I'm Here' tap at 08:42:15, 39 m from pickup, and F2/F5 show the driver within 200 m from 08:41:35 with 5 min 5 s cumulative time; this clause is therefore not available to my client, and my citation of NS-1 in C3 was only to show it does not apply to a rider-cancelled booking.

Conceded on the physical facts: F3 shows the driver stationary 41 m from pickup for 4 min 40 s and F1 a closest approach of 39 m, so the rider's complaint premise that he never arrived is contradicted by the GPS record.

Conceded that the driver communicated and waited (F10, F3); I note only that the tap record is inconsistent (F6 vs F7), which the judge may weigh, but nothing in that inconsistency entitles the rider to a fee reduction under NS-4.
Conceded: F13, F14 and F15 record no traffic incidents, no speed-band records and fair weather, so no external factor excuses the cancellation.

Void as a reasoned point: F16 shows the rider has 1 dispute in 90 days and 0 upheld, which is a neutral profile record and, per the rules, profile facts cannot decide a case; the only effect on the outcome is that no flag_account is sought against my client.

Conceded as framed: NS-0 does route a rider-cancelled on-demand booking to NS-4, and the 3-minute free window is the rider's only rule-based escape — but that window closed at 08:43:00 and the cancellation came at 08:46:40 (F4), so NS-4 does not help her.

Agreed — and this is the driver's own case: the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after the 08:40:00 acceptance (F4) with exactly the published $6.61 fee on record (F8), so NS-4 yields no_action and the driver's record stands.

The driver never needed the no-show route; the point of F1/F2/F3/F5/F6 is only to destroy the complaint's factual premise that 'the driver had not even arrived' — he was within 200 m from 08:41:35, 39 m away at 08:42:40, and stationary 41 m from pickup for 4 min 40 s (F1, F2, F3, F5, F6).

Agreed that a voluntary change of plans gives no waiver — the rider's message 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel' (F11) is her own admission, and NS-4 provides no relief merely because the driver was still en route or waiting.
Agreed: the charge is exactly the published $6.61 (F8) with a 1.0× surge (F9) and no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 has nothing to refund and the rider's overcharge theory fails.

The driver seeks the same substantive result — no_action — so the outcome is not in dispute; NS-7's discretionary voucher channel is a Ryde goodwill matter, and the driver notes the rider's own file shows 0 of 1 disputes upheld in 90 days (F16).
The driver does not seek any adverse action against the rider and requests no flag_account here, so the rider's clean 90-day dispute record (F16) is accepted and irrelevant to the fee's validity.
